newsitem.title: UK: London Stock Exchange to approve new service.
newsitem.headline: London Stock Exchange to approve new service.

text.p: The board of the London Stock Exchange is expected to give the go ahead to the full service definition of the new order-driven trading system when it meets later this week, sources close to the Exchange said.
The new system will bring to an end quote-driven trading where prices are set exclusively by dealers authorised to act as "market-makers".

The changes to the London market come after growing concerns about the competitive pressures from overseas bourses but original expectations of an early summer start for the new service may be disappointed.

In the first round of consultations with the Exchange in January, member firms suggested that nine to 12 months would be needed for the overhaul of the trading system, pushing the start date back to August or September next year.
Originally, the Exchange had hoped to have the new regime in place by Spring 1997.
